scope: Actual candidate DM CLI, real IAM and Ting sandbox, existing shared Ting system daemon, task-owned loopback consumer.

versions.running_daemon_version_evidence: Original process executable resolved to the Ting 0.1.2 package; it was not restarted or upgraded.

preconditions: Task-owned shared test environment and current audience credentials verified by official IAM.
Both recipients had explicit DM delivery registration from the accompanying backend test. Native delivery register was not repeated.
Isolated DM profiles and outgoing relay port; only the task-owned Ting destination was modified.
Documented IAM test-only actor shortcuts used only with verified testing credentials; no production login or send.

checks.name: native_dm_actor_logins
checks.detail: Separate Carbon receiver and Silicon sender DM profiles authenticated using current sandbox app discovery.

checks.name: separate_ting_login
checks.detail: Native delivery login validated the Ting audience, same Carbon actor and kind, live testing environment/generation, and tos organization before retaining the session.

checks.name: direct_all_apps_webhook
checks.detail: Explicit --all-apps attachment directly to the installed shared Ting daemon; task-owned consumer enforces secret, hook, app type, org, environment, generation, and reference identity.

checks.name: native_send_and_authorized_hydration
checks.detail: Candidate CLI sent via DM; authentic Ting callback carried only the reference, and the consumer fetched matching canonical message content through authorized DM HTTP.

checks.name: callback_failure_and_replay
checks.detail: Initial four-item batch replayed with identical delivery IDs after HTTP 503. Scoped reconnect retained the hook ID; its subsequent failed seven-item batch included message 004. A later automatic retry was durably committed and returned 204.

checks.name: stable_hook_reconnect
checks.detail: delivery reconnect retained the exact saved hook and resumed the retained pending batch.

checks.name: consumer_duplicate_handling
checks.scope: local consumer replay of authentic Ting batch
checks.detail: Separate local fixture check replayed an authentic seven-item Ting batch after acceptance; unique delivery IDs prevented any additional durable effects. This check does not claim exactly-once transport.

checks.name: task_hook_queue_drained
checks.detail: Read-only queue verification was restricted to this hook; global pending counts were not used as evidence.

not_covered: Full shared Ting daemon restart was deliberately not attempted.
Explicit delivery registration and backend-originator recovery were covered by the separate parent backend run, not repeated here.
No new isolated-environment clean or app-secret rotation was attempted in this native run.
No production release, deployment, message, or notification.
notes: The first callback arrived before its newly created hook ID file was saved and returned 503 without processing; all replay assertions use subsequent successfully validated and hydrated attempts.
Private fixture data and credentials are retained outside the repository. This report contains no tokens, app secrets, session material, or message body.
